scope: Read-only target-style audit after user rejects overly explicit flu/video replies
user_feedback: Preferred casual friend reply: okok, will do. User concern is excessive formality/explicitness rather than missing empathy or absence of particles.

observations: Original team targets already include terse informal acknowledgments; the entire original dataset is not uniformly formal.

Synthetic additions contain far fewer very short replies and outnumber team examples600to190. This changes the supervised target distribution; it does not causally prove which model behavior it produced.
mT5 A revised targets also reduce short responses63to37 of190; some revisions expand implicit acknowledgments, others preserve short forms such as Swee lah.

Inference receives speaker labels Friend/You; local prompt supplies no explicit relationship/register control beyond these labels. Friend is a generic mapping of peer, including professor conversations.

Original SEA rewrite prompt asks to preserve people, facts, timing and decision; it does not forbid short context-dependent acknowledgment. Target distribution and fidelity interpretation may discourage compression.
Two-stage English-anchored rewriting can encourage explicit semantic restatement, a hypothesis. Okok, will do can preserve the intended commitment through conversational context.
conclusion: Evidence supports a mismatch between desired casual friend texting and parts of the supervised targets/rewrite design. No isolated causal attribution or measured naturalness score established.
recommended_next_step: Audit target register and preserve original terse chat patterns before considering further training. Use varied short replies only where appropriate; preserve explicit amounts/time/negation when needed. Do not add mandatory particles, empathy or a literal okok rule.
